# Workbooks — Learning Center

> Learn Workbooks from zero — 28 plain-language lessons, no technical
> background needed. A graduated path for non-technical people to direct an
> AI agent to build real software, safely. Lessons live at
> https://workbooks.sh/learn/<slug> (clean URLs).

## Unit 1 — Why Workbooks
The shift underneath all of this — and who it changes things for.
- [Why Workbooks](https://workbooks.sh/learn/why-workbooks): The problem/solution case for the ecosystem across people, teams, and organizations — and why this is the durable, future-proof shape, framed indirectly around the shift to directing software rather than hand-building it

## Unit 2 — Build by talking to your agent
Why you can build real software now — and how to do it by describing what you want to an agent that does the building.
- [Why you can build software now](https://workbooks.sh/learn/why-you-can-build-now): The job-to-be-done framing: you don't want 'a workbook', you want software shipped
- [Telling your agent what you want](https://workbooks.sh/learn/tell-it-what-you-want): Level 1->2 of the maturity ladder: describe the outcome, not the implementation; give complete, consistent context; specificity is the single biggest factor in output quality
- [The loop: prompt, look, redirect](https://workbooks.sh/learn/the-loop-prompt-look-redirect): Level 2: iteration is a loop, not one perfect prompt
- [Reading what your agent did](https://workbooks.sh/learn/reading-what-it-did): Level 2->3: review AI work like an untrusted colleague — the sniff-check, spotting drift and failure modes, and the unfakeable ledger as your trustable record
- [Your first workbook, start to finish](https://workbooks.sh/learn/first-workbook-end-to-end): The single worked narrative every analog front-loads and we have zero of: a marketer ships a small tool — prompt -> agent builds -> you review -> ship — told as one continuous story threading the L1->2->3 ladder

## Unit 3 — The whole thing
Now that you've built something, here's what you were standing on — the ecosystem, and the one file you walk away holding.
- [The file you end up holding](https://workbooks.sh/learn/the-one-file): Reframed from 'Foundations = the file' to 'the core unit of an ecosystem
- [The file that remembers how it was made](https://workbooks.sh/learn/carries-its-story): How one artifact carries its own source, identity, and change history so it explains itself and proves where it came from
- [The plain language underneath everything](https://workbooks.sh/learn/the-one-language): Everything in a workbook is written in one human-readable format you could read over someone's shoulder

## Unit 4 — The engine & the sandbox
Why it's safe to hand an agent real power — the runtime you stand on, and the sandbox that means your secrets never touch the OS.
- [Where a workbook comes alive](https://workbooks.sh/learn/coming-alive): The runtime as the load-bearing pillar: a workbook on your laptop is a document; plugged into the engine it answers requests, runs on a schedule, serves people
- [Why a sandbox, not a Mac mini](https://workbooks.sh/learn/why-a-sandbox): The isolation/threat-model story — ~40% of the thesis, currently homeless
- [Giving software powers, safely](https://workbooks.sh/learn/safe-powers): How a workbook gets dangerous-sounding powers (internet, secrets, sending messages) with every power handed over deliberately and revocable
- [Putting it on the internet](https://workbooks.sh/learn/going-live): What deploying actually means and why here it's one push

## Unit 5 — Giving it abilities
How your agent gets real tools to work with — now that you know the engine that runs them safely.
- [Giving a workbook real abilities](https://workbooks.sh/learn/giving-it-abilities): What a toolkit is: existing tools and code safely handed to a workbook so it can DO things without touching your computer
- [When the writing and the program are the same thing](https://workbooks.sh/learn/code-in-the-document): How a document can BE the program — the words a person reads are the instructions the machine runs — and why that makes software you can trust
- [The one command (reference)](https://workbooks.sh/learn/the-one-command): Demoted to a reference card: the AGENT runs wbx, not this non-technical user

## Unit 6 — Agents that work on their own
Once you trust the agent for one task, here's how it works when you're not watching — and how you keep it honest.
- [What an agent really is](https://workbooks.sh/learn/what-an-agent-is): Strip the hype: an agent is a loop — read, act, look at what happened, go again
- [Agents that keep working when you're not watching](https://workbooks.sh/learn/agents-that-persist): How an agent goes from a thing you chat with to a thing that runs on its own — standing watch, taking shifts, resting, and pausing to ask you
- [Knowing whether the agent did well](https://workbooks.sh/learn/did-it-do-well): The deeper review craft: measuring a good job, catching drift, and the record you can't fake

## Unit 7 — Plans that run & the system that improves itself
Your plans become the running work — and the climax: a system that helps improve itself.
- [Plans that run themselves](https://workbooks.sh/learn/plans-that-run): Why your to-do list, calendar, and project board are one plain plan a person reads and a machine carries out
- [When a plan becomes a program](https://workbooks.sh/learn/compiled-plans): The same plan that organizes your week can become a running system with no new tools, and how it changes safely while live
- [The system that improves itself](https://workbooks.sh/learn/the-system-improves-itself): The honest Level-3 summit and the thesis's emotional peak, relocated here from a stray doc-link

## Unit 8 — Trust, sharing & the disk
How something you can copy infinitely stays trustworthy, private, and useful when you hand it out.
- [Proving where it came from](https://workbooks.sh/learn/proving-origin): If anyone can copy a file, how do you know a workbook is really from who it claims? A signature that travels with the bytes and can't be faked
- [Sharing without oversharing](https://workbooks.sh/learn/who-sees-what): A file you send is a file you've given away completely — so how do you share the app without handing over the private data? The public shell vs
- [Keeping a secret inside a file you hand out](https://workbooks.sh/learn/secrets-in-the-open): Part of a file given to everyone can be readable only by the one person holding the right key — locked in the open, opened only on permission
- [A place to keep things that travels with the work](https://workbooks.sh/learn/a-disk-that-travels): Every project needs somewhere to keep files; here it lives inside the workbook, travels when you send it, and can be queried like a spreadsheet
- [When the work outgrows one file](https://workbooks.sh/learn/the-disk-grows): What happens when a project gets big — reaching outside data, remembering by meaning, swapping in real storage — without changing how it works

## Unit 9 — Under the hood
Optional, for the curious — the why behind the magic, and the one idea everything is wearing different clothes of.
- [Why none of this is magic](https://workbooks.sh/learn/under-the-hood): A no-code tour of how the pieces fit — the tiny engine at the center, and the single idea everything is
